chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far from Ayub ibn Nuh from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Regarding the one with a cut horn or a broken horn: if the inner horn is sound, there is no objection, and if the outer visible horn is cut.

key_terms.اَلْمَقْطُوعِ اَلْقَرْنِ: The one with a cut horn
key_terms.اَلْمَكْسُورِ اَلْقَرْنِ: The one with a broken horn
key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: There is no objection/it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sacrificing an animal with a cut or broken horn?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *al-Qarn* (horn) in sacrificial animals, distinguishing between the inner root and the outer visible portion to determine validity. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor physical defects (*‘ayb*) do not invalidate the sacrifice unless they impair the animal's utility or are explicitly prohibited, ensuring the ritual remains accessible while maintaining dignity. This specific ruling underscores the precision of Imami jurisprudence in differentiating between structural integrity and cosmetic appearance in ritual requirements.
